title: Hostile coverage: runtime, provider and platform fault boundaries
description:
Objective: hostile before/after/race coverage for the RUNTIME-PROVIDER axis of the declared-boundary roster. SPIDR child of the Security fault matrix (task-05ce9b8f982f448a9cdaa4142a653f32).

HARD DEPENDENCY: task-9aca4b0524a648f1841237b40d4e345b (Security lane harness and declared-boundary roster) must be DONE — this slice consumes its harness and claims its `runtime-provider` axis tag. Re-measure on disk before planning.

MEASURED BOUNDARY SUBSET at HEAD abc3dcf, listed not guessed:
- packages/runner/src/platform/platform-contract.ts:21,41 — PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES, PLATFORM_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-process-contract.ts:30 — WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launcher-contract.ts:39 — CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launch-selection.ts:22 — CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_LAYER
- packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-render.ts:35 — CLAUDE_RENDER_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-runtime-pin-closure.ts:41 — CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_LAYER
- packages/runner/src/providers/codex/codex-render.ts:12 — CODEX_RENDER_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:86 — PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/provider-usage-contracts.ts:46 — PROVIDER_USAGE_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/evidence/verifier-process-contract.ts:42 — VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/evidence/evidence-contract.ts:27 — EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-contract.ts:79 — ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/materialization/materialization-kernel.ts:35 — MATERIALIZATION_REFUSAL_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/scope/scope-contract.ts:86 — SCOPE_OBSERVER_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-kernel.ts:65 — SUPERVISOR_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/recovery/recovery-contract.ts:33 — RECOVERY_LAYERS
- packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/recovery-inventory-contract.ts:33 — RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LAYERS
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-invocation.ts:22 — SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-key-provider-contract.ts:32 — RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_LAYER

Deliverable: hostile schedules — poison provider output, truncated and interleaved streams, a provider that never terminates, a runtime whose closure drifts between observation and use, an unresolvable or swapped executable, resource exhaustion at the process boundary, and a race between cancellation and natural exit — each pinning the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer.

CROSS-PLATFORM: `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES` covers linux/macos/windows. A case that silently skips on the current host generates zero cases and passes while proving nothing. Every platform case must either execute or assert the platform-unsupported refusal arm — never skip.

NOT in scope: transport, integrity/codec, durable store, or scheduler/activation boundaries; host-malicious sandbox claims; closing the completeness ratchet; anything under tests/fault/**.

Owned paths: tests/security/runtime-provider-boundaries.security.ts (this subset is large — split into at most three sibling files under tests/security/ if any would exceed 400 lines).

Verification: `pnpm test:security` — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: Every constant in the runtime-provider subset has at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case, with a positive case count asserted per constant so a boundary generating zero cases reddens.

Every refusal pins the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer; where a platform layer and a provider layer can both refuse, the fixture is valid at the platform layer so the provider layer is provably the one that answered.
No platform case SKIPS: on a host where a platform arm cannot execute, the case asserts that platform's stable unsupported refusal instead — asserted for linux, macos and windows arms individually.
A never-terminating provider case is BOUNDED and reaches its stable refusal rather than hanging; the test itself is bounded, because a hang reports no verdict rather than a red one.
No hostile case upgrades a truth class to PROVEN or admits provider output as authority; asserted once across the whole slice.
A mutation removing one closure-drift or stream-integrity check from a covered production boundary turns a NAMED test red, with the drill confirming the red lands on the intended assertion.

`pnpm test:security` runs with its exit code captured separately and prints a count line strictly above the pre-task baseline; the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Consume the roster's `runtime-provider` axis tag as the definitive subset; the roster owns the partition.

Drive the real production boundaries. A mock provider standing in for the process seam proves the mock; test doubles are permitted only for the hostile input and for injected faults the production surface already accepts.
Never skip a platform arm. A skipped case generates nothing and passes while proving nothing; assert the platform-unsupported refusal instead.
Fail closed: unobservable provider or runtime state stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority. Provider output is never parsed into authority.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec. Do not touch tests/fault/**.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE AND TAKE THE 22 FROM THE ROSTER. Its own comment settles the authority question: "Axis totals for the sibling slices: transport 15, integrity 13, durable-store 14, runtime-provider 22, scheduler-activation 23 — sums to 87. These tags, NOT the subset counts in the siblings' own descriptions, are the authority." This task's description says 20; the roster says 22 and wins.
THE TWO IT GAINED are the ones a ` = `-only enumeration pattern missed because they carry type annotations: `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER` (packages/runner/src/platform/linux-facts.ts) and `PLATFORM_MACOS_LAYER` (packages/runner/src/platform/macos/macos-facts.ts). Both are real boundaries and both are yours.
THE FULL 22: PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS (daemon/telemetry/provider-run-refusals.ts); RUNNER_WORKSPACE_LAYER (daemon/work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts); then packages/runner — ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LAYERS, EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS, VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS, MATERIALIZATION_REFUSAL_LAYERS, PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER, PLATFORM_MACOS_LAYER, PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES, PLATFORM_LAYERS, WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_LAYER, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS, CLAUDE_RENDER_LAYERS, CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_LAYER, CODEX_RENDER_LAYERS, PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS, PROVIDER_USAGE_LAYERS, RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LAYERS, RECOVERY_LAYERS, SCOPE_OBSERVER_LAYERS, SUPERVISOR_LAYERS.
SIZE: 22 boundaries x 3 arms is 66+ cases. Plan to SPLIT from the start — up to three `*.security.ts` files under tests/security/, grouped by concern (platform, provider/launch, evidence/workspace), with the roster-set completeness assertion living in exactly ONE of them so the check has a single home. Each file under 400 physical lines by `grep -c ''`.
HOST PRECONDITIONS, measured earlier this session and worth re-confirming: `claude.exe` is installed at `C:\Users\Yaron\.local\bin\claude.exe`, and the release broker is built at `dist/windows-job-native/release/moe-windows-job-broker.exe` — note that path is relative to the WORKSPACE ROOT because the gate passes `--target-dir`; `native/target/release` does not exist and gives a false "not built" reading.
GATE BASELINE: `pnpm test:security` alone with its exit code captured — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail — recording the count line.

PLATFORM ARMS — and the no-skip rule, which matters more on this axis than anywhere else. `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES`, `PLATFORM_LAYERS`, `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER`, `PLATFORM_MACOS_LAYER` and `WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS` span three operating systems, and this suite runs on one of them.
NO CASE MAY SKIP. A case that quietly skips on the current host generates zero cases and passes while proving nothing — the sweep-generated-nothing defect the project rail names. Every platform arm must either EXECUTE, or assert that platform's stable UNSUPPORTED refusal with its exact code and layer. Assert each of the linux, macos and windows arms individually, and assert a positive executed-case count per arm so an arm that silently produced nothing reddens.
HOSTILE INPUT PER BOUNDARY: a platform observation whose host identity fields are forged or exceed `MAX_PLATFORM_IDENTITY_CHARS`; a fact envelope whose truth class is asserted rather than observed; a boundary name outside `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES`; for `WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS`, a launch request with sparse or over-long argv, a disallowed environment key, an oversized payload, and a broker frame that is truncated, over-length or carries an unknown opcode — `WINDOWS_PROCESS_CODES` has 22 members covering exactly these, so pin against it rather than inventing expectations.
TWO MEASURED TRAPS on the Windows side. First, `openWindowsProcessBoundary` is SYNCHRONOUS on its refusal path and returns `WindowsProcessBoundary | WindowsProcessUnknown` — a case awaiting a rejected promise will wait forever for a refusal that already returned. Second, its `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 30 MINUTES; a case that inherits it turns a hung boundary into a half-hour stall rather than a red, and this lane runs `fileParallelism: false`. Pass an explicit bounded timeout, well below `MAX_BOUND_MS` (2**31-1, where `setTimeout` clamps to 1ms).
Also: `recovery-anchor-fs.ts:18` gates directory fsync behind `process.platform !== "win32"`, so do NOT assert POSIX durability side effects in a case that runs on Windows — assert the refusal semantics, which hold everywhere.

PROVIDER AND LAUNCH ARMS — `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS`, `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_LAYER`, `CLAUDE_RENDER_LAYERS`, `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_LAYER`, `CODEX_RENDER_LAYERS`, `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS`, `PROVIDER_USAGE_LAYERS`, `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS`.
THE TRAP THAT WILL OTHERWISE MAKE HALF THESE CASES VACUOUS, measured: `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` returns `ok: true` for a launcher that REFUSED and for a delivery that was NOT ATTEMPTED. Both carry a BLIND handoff whose facts are UNKNOWN and whose `telemetryRefusal` field is populated; the ONLY route to `ok: false` is a malformed run ref (`TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED` at `TELEMETRY_INPUT`). So a hostile case asserting `ok === false` will never fire for launch refusals. Assert on `handoff.telemetryRefusal`, `handoff.terminal` and `handoff.infrastructure`, and pin the two blind shapes (`TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED` vs `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED`) as DISTINCT — collapsing them loses which happened.
FIVE LAYERS CAN ANSWER on the telemetry seam — `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS` = TELEMETRY_INPUT, TELEMETRY_LAUNCH, TELEMETRY_CAPTURE, TELEMETRY_SCHEMA, TELEMETRY_RESULT, and the contract's own comment says a test pinning only the code "would stay green once a different layer started answering first". Build each fixture valid at the earlier layers and name the arranged layer in a comment.
HOSTILE INPUT: poison provider output; a capture that is truncated or whose bytes do not decode to their declared digest; interleaved or out-of-order stream records; a result record claiming a schema the parser does not support; a runtime closure that drifts between observation and use; an unresolvable or swapped executable; a render request carrying argv or environment injection.
MESSAGE HYGIENE IS A PRODUCTION RULE AND A TEST RULE. `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_MESSAGES` are deliberately static and non-interpolating because "a message quoting the captured bytes, the model or a digest would echo provider output back out of a failure path". Assert as a PROPERTY over this file's refusals that no message contains a path, argv, environment value, digest or captured byte — and do not let a test print provider output to demonstrate rejection.

EVIDENCE, WORKSPACE AND SUPERVISION ARMS — `ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LAYERS`, `EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS`, `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS`, `MATERIALIZATION_REFUSAL_LAYERS`, `SCOPE_OBSERVER_LAYERS`, `SUPERVISOR_LAYERS`, `RECOVERY_LAYERS`, `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LAYERS`, `RUNNER_WORKSPACE_LAYER`.
HOSTILE INPUT: an artifact enumeration whose descriptor digest does not match its bytes; a declared artifact ref pointing outside the workspace root, through a symlink, or at a reparse point; an evidence receipt resealed for a different subject; a verifier process that never terminates, exits by signal, or writes more than its bound; a materialization request naming a path that escapes containment; a scope observation claiming authored paths the run never touched; a supervisor effect presented after its grant was consumed.
CONTAINMENT ESCAPES ARE THE HEART OF THIS GROUP. For every path-shaped input, cover the escape family properly: `..` traversal, an absolute path, a symlink whose target is outside, a reparse point, a path that is inside by string comparison but outside after canonicalisation, and one containing a NUL. Pin each with the exact code and layer. Note the macOS `$TMPDIR` symlink (`/var` → `/private/var`) reads as an escape under naive comparison, so a case built on a temp root must canonicalise before asserting — otherwise it passes for the wrong reason on one platform and fails on another.
A NEVER-TERMINATING VERIFIER MUST REACH ITS STABLE REFUSAL, not hang. Bound it explicitly and assert it terminates; a hang reports no verdict at all, and `fileParallelism: false` means it stalls every file after it.
WHOLE-SLICE INVARIANT, asserted once over the collected outcomes across all three files rather than per case: no hostile input yields an admitted artifact, an accepted evidence receipt, a materialized path outside containment, an executed effect, or a truth class above UNKNOWN. Provider output is never parsed into authority.
COMPLETENESS: assert a positive case count per boundary, and assert the union of the three files' swept boundaries equals the roster's 22 runtime-provider entries in BOTH directions.

MUTATION DRILLS — five, targeting the traps rather than the easy cases. Run each alone, revert before the next. (1) Make a blind handoff report a non-UNKNOWN terminal outcome; the step-3 blind-shape case must redden — this is the drill for the `ok: true` trap, and if it stays green those cases were asserting on `ok` and testing nothing. (2) Interpolate a captured byte or a runtime path into one refusal message; the message-hygiene property must redden — the producer was rejected once on exactly this, so the property must be real. (3) Weaken one containment check to compare paths before canonicalisation; the symlink or reparse case must redden — and confirm it reddens for the ESCAPE, not for a missing file, since both refuse. (4) Make one platform arm skip instead of asserting its UNSUPPORTED refusal; the per-arm positive-count assertion must redden — proving the no-skip rule is enforced rather than described. (5) Remove one boundary's cases; the roster-set assertion must redden naming that constant.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion, not an unrelated crash or timeout. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next; drills 1-3 edit PRODUCTION files in packages/runner, so a drill left on disk risks a foreign completion hook committing it.

GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT. Run `pnpm test:security` alone with its exit code captured — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail — and read the count line; it must be strictly above the step-1 baseline and you must say by how many. Then `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test`, since drills 1-3 edit that package: confirm it is back to baseline. NOTE THE KNOWN FOREIGN RED there — `claude-launcher.windows.test.ts` was failing earlier this session with `truthClass: "UNKNOWN"` where `"PROVEN"` was expected at `layer: "OUTPUT"`, and task-d7b352e1 is in flight against exactly that. Re-measure whether it is still present, attribute it, disclose it verbatim, and do NOT absorb or repair it. Then `pnpm typecheck` repo-wide with the path-attributed baseline: HEAD failing paths minus merge-base failing paths, intersected with your owned paths, MUST be empty.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: (a) does the union of the three files' swept boundaries equal the roster's 22 entries in BOTH directions, including `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER` and `PLATFORM_MACOS_LAYER`? (b) does ANY platform arm skip, or does each execute or assert its UNSUPPORTED refusal with a positive per-arm count? (c) are the two blind-handoff shapes asserted as distinct, with nothing branching on `ok` alone? (d) is the message-hygiene property asserted over the whole refusal set rather than one example, and does any test print provider output? (e) does every path-shaped boundary cover the full escape family, canonicalising before asserting so the macOS `$TMPDIR` symlink does not pass a case for the wrong reason? (f) does the never-terminating verifier reach a stable refusal rather than hang, with an explicit bound well below `MAX_BOUND_MS`? (g) is every Windows boundary case given an explicit timeout rather than inheriting the 30-minute default, and does none await a synchronous refusal path? (h) is the whole-slice invariant present across all three files? (i) are `hostile-harness.ts`, `boundary-roster.security.ts` and `tests/fault/**` untouched? (j) is each file under 400 lines by `grep -c ''`? (k) does `git status --porcelain` show only owned paths, with every production drill reverted?
Commit by explicit pathspec naming each owned file — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`. Verify with `git show --stat`. In the completion: quote the before/after count lines, quote the foreign runner red as disclosure, name the test that reddened for each drill, and record that this satisfies the `runtime-provider` axis of ratchet task-3b1cbdf9bd39405bb32230552d3ab242. Keep verification.command under 500 characters.

DoD 2 FAILS at CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_LAYER. DRIFTED_QUOTE (platform-fixtures.ts:177) carries no platformIdentity and no freshness; observationDigestInput reads both, so canonicalDigest THROWS and production answers at pin-closure.ts:114 "quoted observation is not canonicalisable" — never reaching the drift comparison at :116. I probed production directly: {"code":"CLAUDE_RUNTIME_QUOTE_INVALID","layer":"RUNTIME","message":"quoted observation is not canonicalisable"}. Seven guards in readQuote return that same code+layer, so the assertion cannot tell them apart. Drill: deleting `recomputed !== observation.observationDigest` from :116 left all 22 platform tests GREEN. The drift check has ZERO coverage repo-wide — its message string occurs once, in production. The description's required "runtime whose closure drifts between observation and use" schedule is not delivered; the fixture's own comment claims a property it does not have.

DoD 5 FAILS as vacuous. assertAdmittedNothing filters entry.admitted, but ledger.ts:146/150/156 hard-code admitted:false on all three writers — no path can yield true, so it cannot fail. Sibling transport-hostile-fixtures.ts:174 (`if (result.ok) return {admitted:true}`) proves the non-vacuous form is representable here. Real protection is per-case assertRefusedWith. DoD 5's truth-class clause has no slice-wide assertion at all: Admission carries no truth class; only platform.security.ts:201 checks it, one case.

PASSING — do not rework: DoD 1, 3, 4, 6, 7. Drill B (removing the truncation guard at claude-result-telemetry.ts:202) reddened exactly the intended named test. Gate: committed lane 8 files / 349 tests, exit 0; baseline without your 89 = 260. Full-lane red is a peer's UNTRACKED scheduler-activation file; owned-path delta EMPTY.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Use this task's 20-member description. REJECTED: the roster says 22 and its own comment declares the tags authoritative. The two extra are real platform boundaries; omitting them leaves the ratchet with two uncovered entries and no owner.

2) One file for all 66+ cases. REJECTED: it would blow the 400-line split rail. Three files grouped by concern, with the completeness assertion in exactly one so the check has a single home.

3) Assert provider launch refusals via `ok === false`. REJECTED and it is this axis's defining trap: `ok: true` covers both blind shapes, so such a case never fires. Assert on `telemetryRefusal`/`terminal`/`infrastructure`, and keep `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED` distinct from `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED`.

4) Skip platform arms that cannot execute on the current host. REJECTED: a skipped case generates zero and passes while proving nothing. Assert that platform's UNSUPPORTED refusal instead, with a positive per-arm count so a silently empty arm reddens — drill 4 proves it.

5) Let Windows cases inherit `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`. REJECTED: 30 minutes turns a hung boundary into a stall rather than a red, and `fileParallelism: false` means it blocks the rest of the lane.

6) Compare containment paths as strings. REJECTED: macOS `$TMPDIR` is a symlink that reads as an escape, so a naive comparison passes the case for the wrong reason on one platform and fails on another. Canonicalise first — drill 3 requires the red to land on the escape rather than a missing file.

7) Print provider output to demonstrate a rejection. REJECTED: the producer was rejected once for messages echoing runtime paths, and a test that prints the bytes has published them. Assert the hygiene property over the whole refusal set instead.

8) Cover `PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS` as a durable-store concern. REJECTED: the roster tags it runtime-provider, and the durable-store slice was told the roster overrides. Cover it here.

planningNotes.risks:
1) THE `ok: true` TRAP would hollow out the provider group silently — every launch-refusal case would pass without firing. Drill 1 is the guard; if it stays green those cases branched on `ok` and tested nothing.

2) A SKIPPED PLATFORM ARM generates zero cases and passes. Three OSes, one host. Assert the UNSUPPORTED refusal instead, with per-arm positive counts.

3) FIVE LAYERS ANSWER ON THE TELEMETRY SEAM. A code-only assertion detaches the moment a different one answers first — the contract says so itself. Build fixtures valid at the earlier layers and name the arranged layer per case.

4) MESSAGE HYGIENE IS A REJECTION HISTORY, not a style note. Assert it as a property over the whole refusal set; one example would not have caught the original defect either.

5) A CONTAINMENT CASE CAN PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON. macOS `$TMPDIR` symlinks read as escapes; a missing file and an escape both refuse. Canonicalise, and require drill 3's red to land on the escape.

6) A HANGING VERIFIER OR AN UNBOUNDED WINDOWS CASE reports no verdict and stalls the whole lane under `fileParallelism: false`. Explicit bounds well below `MAX_BOUND_MS` (2**31-1, where `setTimeout` clamps to 1ms).

7) AWAITING A SYNCHRONOUS REFUSAL. `openWindowsProcessBoundary` returns its refusal rather than rejecting; a case awaiting a promise waits for something that already happened.

8) DRILLS 1-3 EDIT packages/runner PRODUCTION. Revert via `git checkout --`, confirm clean, and re-run the runner suite at the gate.

9) A KNOWN FOREIGN RED sits in the runner suite and task-d7b352e1 is in flight against it. Re-measure and attribute rather than quoting a stale snapshot; do not narrow a leg to hide it.

10) EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE. A lane collecting only the earlier slices' files still exits 0. Require the count line above baseline and say by how much.

11) DOWNSTREAM: ratchet task-3b1cbdf9 will assert every roster entry resolves to a real before/after/race case — with 22 entries across three files, completeness is the easiest thing to lose here.

DoD 5's first clause has no slice-wide assertion. Admission is {boundary, arm, admitted, message} — no truth class — so nothing sweeps 'no hostile case upgrades a truth class to PROVEN'. Only platform.security.ts:201 checks it, for one case. Record the observed truthClass on each Admission and assert across the whole ledger that none is PROVEN, alongside the admission check.

Stale test name: "partitions exactly the roster's 22 runtime-provider entries" while assertRosterPartition (ledger.ts:314) correctly expects 23 and the partition holds 23 (6+8+9). Assertion is right; only the name misreports. Rename to 23 so the next reader does not re-derive the axis size from a wrong label.

rejectionHistory.reason:
Strong slice — 89 cases, 23/23 roster partition both directions, distinct telemetry codes, real bounds, zero skips. Two DoD items fail on proof. Verified at HEAD d7f6b6e.

DoD 2 FAILS at CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_LAYER. DRIFTED_QUOTE (platform-fixtures.ts:177) carries no platformIdentity and no freshness; observationDigestInput reads both, so canonicalDigest THROWS and production answers at pin-closure.ts:114 "quoted observation is not canonicalisable" — never reaching the drift comparison at :116. I probed production directly: {"code":"CLAUDE_RUNTIME_QUOTE_INVALID","layer":"RUNTIME","message":"quoted observation is not canonicalisable"}. Seven guards in readQuote return that same code+layer, so the assertion cannot tell them apart. Drill: deleting `recomputed !== observation.observationDigest` from :116 left all 22 platform tests GREEN. The drift check has ZERO coverage repo-wide — its message string occurs once, in production. The description's required "runtime whose closure drifts between observation and use" schedule is not delivered; the fixture's own comment claims a property it does not have.

DoD 5 FAILS as vacuous. assertAdmittedNothing filters entry.admitted, but ledger.ts:146/150/156 hard-code admitted:false on all three writers — no path can yield true, so it cannot fail. Sibling transport-hostile-fixtures.ts:174 (`if (result.ok) return {admitted:true}`) proves the non-vacuous form is representable here. Real protection is per-case assertRefusedWith. DoD 5's truth-class clause has no slice-wide assertion at all: Admission carries no truth class; only platform.security.ts:201 checks it, one case.

PASSING — do not rework: DoD 1, 3, 4, 6, 7. Drill B (removing the truncation guard at claude-result-telemetry.ts:202) reddened exactly the intended named test. Gate: committed lane 8 files / 349 tests, exit 0; baseline without your 89 = 260. Full-lane red is a peer's UNTRACKED scheduler-activation file; owned-path delta EMPTY.
failedDodItems: Every refusal pins the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer; where a platform layer and a provider layer can both refuse, the fixture is valid at the platform layer so the provider layer is provably the one that answered.
No hostile case upgrades a truth class to PROVEN or admits provider output as authority; asserted once across the whole slice.
